$comment: Rule catalog — computational and numerical evidence, finite reasoning, error bounds. Standards 10, 11, 12, 13.

rules.title: A computation records what it checked
rules.description: Evidence of type computational or numerical records the predicate checked, the range or sample, the arithmetic used, the program, the environment, any seed, and the outcome.
rules.rationale: Almost every dispute about a computational result turns out to be a dispute about one of these lines, and none of them requires mathematical judgement to record.
rules.remediation: Expand the evidence entry to cover Standard 10 R1's seven items, and commit the script rather than describing it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Looks for a bound and an arithmetic declaration in the evidence text. It cannot confirm that the program checked what the entry says it checked.

rules.title: A cited computation exists in the repository
rules.description: A path-shaped artifact named by computational or numerical evidence resolves to a file in the repository.
rules.rationale: A computation described but not committed cannot be re-run, and a result nobody can re-run is an assertion.
rules.remediation: Commit the script and its log, and cite the path.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a file is present at the cited path. It does not run it, and does not check that the committed script is the one that produced the reported output.

rules.title: Approximations carry error bounds
rules.description: A claim stating an approximate value, a truncation, or an asymptotic relation states the error bound and what establishes it.
rules.rationale: An approximation without a bound is a number with no claim attached; the same notation is used for a rigorous bound, a heuristic estimate, and a value read off a plot.
rules.remediation: State the bound, its magnitude, whether it is rigorous or estimated, and what proves it — in the Statement field, not only in the computation's output.
rules.$assuranceNote: A pattern match over informal mathematical prose, imperfect in both directions: it misses an unbounded approximation written without a marker, and may flag a bound expressed in a form it does not recognise. Findings are INFERRED.

rules.title: Numerical evidence is never presented as deductive proof
rules.description: A claim at proved rank has no evidence of type proof, formal, or citation — its support is entirely computational, numerical, symbolic, or heuristic.
rules.rationale: Computation is the best source of mathematical intuition ever built and it proves almost nothing. The gap between COMPUTATIONAL_VERIFICATION and LEMMA is the line this framework is built around.
rules.remediation: Lower the status to COMPUTATIONAL_VERIFICATION or NUMERICAL_OBSERVATION, or restate the claim on the range the computation covered — where it is then a genuine theorem whose proof is the exhaustive computation.
rules.$assuranceNote: The ledger arm is exact over declared evidence types. A second arm matches phrasings such as 'proved numerically' in prose and reports INFERRED, never OBSERVED — reporting a phrase match as an observation would be this tool committing the error it is checking for. Neither arm detects a deductive-looking proof that is secretly empirical.

rules.title: An infinite claim never rests solely on finitely many cases
rules.description: A claim at proved rank is universally quantified over an unbounded domain and its evidence describes a bounded range, with no proof or formal artifact cited.
rules.rationale: Mertens held for everything anyone could compute and is false. Pólya was verified into the hundreds of millions and fails at 906,150,257. The size of a finite search carries no information about what happens past its bound.
rules.remediation: Restate the claim on the range checked, or lower it to CONJECTURE with the computation as supporting evidence. Both are honest; stating both, with the conjecture citing the theorem, is usually best.
rules.$assuranceNote: Both halves are pattern matches over informal text, so findings are INFERRED. A claim whose universal quantification is implicit in prose and absent from the field is not caught, and a subtly incomplete reduction argument shows a proof evidence entry and stays quiet. What it reliably catches is the unguarded case: a big computation, a universal statement, and nothing in between.

rules.title: Floating-point output is never exact mathematics
rules.description: Evidence declaring exact arithmetic cites a program that uses floating-point arithmetic, or a claim of exact equality rests on a floating-point comparison.
rules.rationale: A computation reporting agreement to fifteen decimal places has established that two quantities are close, which is a statement about the computation and not about the quantities.
rules.remediation: Use exact integer or rational arithmetic, or interval arithmetic with the interval reported, or supply an error analysis bounding the gap between what was computed and what was meant.
rules.$assuranceNote: A heuristic scan of the cited script for floating-point constructs, reported INFERRED. It cannot tell whether a float appears in the part of the program that matters, and it does not detect exactness claims resting on a computation that was never committed.

rules.title: Computational results are never cherry-picked
rules.description: The reported computation describes the parameter ranges where the pattern held while omitting ranges that were tested and did not.
rules.rationale: No single case is concealed — only the shape of the search — which is why it reads as a complete report and is not one.
rules.remediation: Report the full search, including the ranges that failed, and keep the failed runs in the repository.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector and there cannot be one: selective reporting is a property of what was omitted, and omissions leave no artifact. Established by a reviewer comparing reported runs against the runs the repository still contains, which is why Standard 18 requires failures to be preserved.

rules.title: Computer algebra output is a claim, not an oracle
rules.description: A CAS simplification, solution, or closed form is used without checking the validity conditions the system assumed and did not report.
rules.rationale: Simplification assumes genericity, chooses principal branches, discards measure-zero cases, and cancels factors without recording the excluded values. Its contract is 'return something equal under conditions I will not tell you'.
rules.remediation: Record the CAS result at HEURISTIC rank until its conditions are checked; name the system and version, and verify by substitution or an independent route.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Establishing which assumptions a simplification made requires re-deriving it.
